newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil markets very quiet, outlook unsettled.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil markets very quiet, outlook unsettled.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets were quiet on Friday with barge prices static and cargo trade moribund.
A few high sulphur barges were traded at $82 and $82.50 fob ARA, but hardly enough to shake the market from its lethargy.
"It's unbelievably quiet, a really boring market," said one trader. "Prices are really stuck in a range and I hope they break out, up or down."
Dealers said they were amazed at how quiet the week was, with bunker demand running below average.
"It's been a very strange and difficult week, with a great deal of uncertainty in it," said one trader.

Barges hit a high of $87 on Tuesday and a low of $79.50 on Wednesday in very thin trade before settling down to move in a narrow range. Barge dealers said much of the movement had been manipulative, with little fundamental reasons beneath it.
Worries that Singapore's buying spree might end and falling prices there would depress Euro product values were also lending a bearish tone to some outlooks.
High and low sulphur cargo markets were deadly dull.
